answer: Each agent stakes a bond that a peer committee can seize if its work fails verification. A Sybil farmer spinning up a thousand identities must post that stake a thousand times before any earns a grain, so the attack becomes capital-bound rather than cheap. Consensus weight scales with bonded value plus decaying reputation, so fresh keys start near empty and hold no beacon of trust to borrow; a crowd of them looks hollow. The ledger records each bond as a permanent umber mark, making recycled keys visible. Attacker cost rises linearly while payout stays flat.
